summary: The board-specific logic is mostly MAME's polepos driver turned into RTL. The sprite and road engines are line-buffer FSMs that walk the same loops as zoom_sprite/draw_sprites and draw_road, using the same expressions (sx=pos-0x40+4, sy=513-pos, the siz+=1+sizex DDA, romoffs/bits2 address folding, a 264-pixel scanline read at an xscroll offset). Layers are combined in screen_update order (bg|road, sprites, tx) through four separate palette modules that use MAME's indirect-pen offsets, not one colour PROM fed by a priority encoder. The 06xx, the 53xx steering, IC25, the watchdog and the engine-sound filters are also MAME device or handler code in RTL form. The one hardware-leaning part is the per-pixel tile fetch pipeline driven by H/V counters.

findings.note: The FSM goes through sprites 0..63 reading attributes at 0x380/0x780 with stride 2. It computes sx=p1w-0x40+4 and sy=513-pos. It runs the same inner loop: x counts 0x40/0x20, dy=scalelut[(y<<6)+sizey] with >>1 for small sprites, col=(offs>>1)^offsxor (0x1f/0x0f), and the siz+=1+sizex, if(siz&0x40) xx++ DDA. All of these match MAME term for term.

findings.signal: road generator transliterates draw_road incl. MAME buffer artifact
findings.note: The states compute yoffs=((vposmod[y]+vscroll)>>3)&0x1ff, roadpal=mem[yoffs]&15 and xoffs=mem[0x380+y]. They then loop 33 chunks of 8 pixels with the xoffs&0x200 fill, romoffs=((y&7f)<<6)+((xoffs&1f8)>>3), b2off=(romoffs&fff)|((romoffs&1000)>>1), and 'if(!carin&&bits) bits++'. Output reads the 264-entry scanline at hpos+xscroll, which reproduces MAME's scanline[256+8] / &scanline[xscroll] trick.

Final RGB is picked by muxing already-converted per-layer RGB: view if vpos<128 else road, then sprite, then alpha. That is MAME's draw order (bg clipped to y<=127, road, sprites, tx). The board instead uses a priority encoder that drives MUX/ALPHA-BACK/SPRITE-BACK into one shared colour PROM.

findings.signal: per-layer palettes mirror MAME's indirect-pen tables
findings.note: Each layer has its own copy of the R/G/B PROMs and adds MAME's set_pen_indirect bases (0x20/0x60 for alpha, 0x10/0x50 for sprites, 0x40 for road). Each runs the 0x0e/0x1f/0x43/0x8f weights as a function, and transparency is tested as promval==15. This is MAME's colortable layout, not the board's shared colour-PROM address.

findings.signal: 06xx is a port of the MAME device's timer model
findings.note: It has MAME's state variables (timer_state, read_stretch, ctrl[7:5] divisor 1<<n, chipsel=ctrl&timer_state). Reads AND-reduce the selected chips with 0xFF defaults and return 0 in write mode, as data_r does. The deferred ctrl/data writes stand in for scheduler synchronize(). The chip's serial shift interface is not modelled.

The registers steer_last/steer_accum/steer_delta use MAME's member names. The update is accum += (new-last)*2, then +1/-1 toward zero with delta set to 0/1, and R0=accum&1. This is the emulator's synthetic quadrature model fed into the MCU ports.

findings.signal: IC25 protection and READY/IRQ handlers as MAME callbacks
findings.note: IC25 keeps last_signed/last_unsigned/last_result and multiplies a signed 8-bit value by an unsigned 8-bit value, as polepos2_ic25_r does. READY is written as 0xFF ^ 0x02(vpos>=128) ^ 0x08(!intr), and the IRQs fire on vpos==64/192/240 equality tests. Both are the handler code in RTL, not 64V/128V counter-bit gating.
A 4-bit counter counts vpos==240 events and fires a reset pulse on the 16th. This is MAME's watchdog_timer_device setting, not a counter clocked from a board raster bit.

findings.signal: engine sound reproduces polepos_sound_device incl. biquad contexts
findings.note: It keeps MAME's sample_msb/lsb (data&62, data&63) and a ((msb+1)*64+lsb+1)-style step accumulator indexed by position>>12. Volume comes from an 8-slot table, and three cascaded filters use x0/x1/x2/y1/y2 state with bilinear coefficients. This is MAME's software filter model, not a model of the discrete circuit.

findings.signal: per-pixel tile fetch pipeline from H/V counters
findings.note: Tiles are fetched one 8-pixel span ahead, with gfx bytes read at fixed pixel phases and latched at p==7. The 128V bank comes from vpos[7] rather than MAME's tile_index>=32*16. The scan order is still parameterised as MAME's TILEMAP_SCAN_ROWS/COLS with 32x32/64x16 dimensions.

findings.signal: VRAM split, LS259 latch and memory maps
findings.note: The four word RAMs (sprite/road/alpha/view), the address decodes, the LS259 bit-addressed latch and the NVI enable latch are shared knowledge that any correct core must match. The time-sliced three-CPU arbitration is FPGA engineering.
